html:
SMTO-ART-0021 — Files can only be saved during a Task

GUID: 15d82b8f-3b97-4fec-b25f-de9d8bb8003f
Slug: artifact-run-required
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO tried to save or list files from a step that isn't connected to a Task, so there was nowhere to keep them. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In a conversation, send a new message asking SMTO to create or save the file. Each message starts a Task, and every Task has its own place to keep saved files.
  2. When the Task finishes, open Artifacts from this run to check that the file is there. Files saved during a Task are listed there for viewing and download.

What success looks like

  • The file appears in Artifacts from this run for the new Task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying where you started the request. Don't copy the file into another Task's folder by hand.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An artifact.* capability ran without an artifact registry (_artifact_store) in its execution context, so no durable run namespace was bound for listing or registration.

What this means

  • The artifact capability receives no artifact registry in its execution context before listing or registration. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • The artifact capability receives no artifact registry in its execution context before listing or registration.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect owning run initialization and workspace context rather than creating an unrelated directory.

How to fix it

  • artifact.* tools require a native run bound by agent_runtime/artifacts/runtime.bind, which native/state.py calls during run setup. Use the operation's trace and the Server log to find which execution path invoked the tool without that binding, and route it through a native run instead of registering into another run's namespace.
  • Register the artifact from the owning active durable task and workspace.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended active durable task exposes its supported artifact registry.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
